curriculum.lesson_evidence: Choosing a research topic means picking something interesting, narrow enough to manage and possible to research with available sources.
curriculum.scope_limit: Single lesson: partial evidence. Cross-check existing card mapping and NESA content point.

lesson.child_mission: Choosing a research topic means picking something interesting, narrow enough to manage and possible to research with available sources.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same strategy to an unfamiliar topic or audience, then compare the effect of two different choices.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Sort: (1) dinosaurs (2) How do kangaroo joeys grow in the pouch? Which is a better focused topic and why?

FEEDBACK
Focused question (2) is better for a short report; (1) is too broad without narrowing.

CHECK
A topic with no available kid-friendly sources will stall the project.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
List five interesting topics, narrow each to a how/why question, rate sources you can actually find and choose one research question for the unit.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Choosing a research topic means picking something interesting, narrow enough to manage and possible to research with available sources.
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: List five interesting topics, narrow each to a how/why question, rate sources you can actually find and choose one research question for the unit. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: original example using topic on new material; names a specific word, source or choice and explains its effect.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample error: A topic with no available kid-friendly sources will stall the project.. Correction: Focused question (2) is better for a short report;. Why it helps the audience is stated.

Parent: Likely misconception: A topic with no available kid-friendly sources will stall the project. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating topic on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with topic, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept original work about topic with a specific supporting detail. Reject copied model wording with no new material. / Accept a misconception, a correction, and a purpose-linked reason for topic. Reject corrections that do not change the inaccurate idea..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
"How honeybees find flowers" is more researchable for Year 3 than "everything about insects". Interest + focus + sources.

TRY FIRST
Sort: (1) dinosaurs (2) How do kangaroo joeys grow in the pouch? Which is a better focused topic and why?

FEEDBACK
Focused question (2) is better for a short report; (1) is too broad without narrowing.
teach_steps.explain:
Choosing a research topic means picking something interesting, narrow enough to manage and possible to research with available sources.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
teach_steps.notice: A topic with no available kid-friendly sources will stall the project. Correct the meaning, not just the appearance.
teach_steps.title: Understand and model
